mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month (as measured by the change in FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS decline are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a robust labor market and strong consumer demand, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE < 3.6 and HOUST > 1300 are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and CPIAUCSL > 250), aggressive rate hikes and persistent inflation expectations compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and CPIAUCSL > 250 are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with GDPC1 growth rate > 1.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
